training_dataset: UCI Default of Credit Card Clients

preprocessing.description: numeric: median imputation (+binary missing indicators for columns with missing values in TRAIN) then standard scaling; categorical: most-frequent imputation then one-hot encoding (handle_unknown='ignore'). Fitted on TRAIN ONLY inside the pipeline; validation/test transformed frozen.

inference.input: pandas.DataFrame with exactly the columns and order in feature_columns.json
inference.output: predicted probability of default next month in [0, 1]; multiply by 100 for the 0-100 risk score; bands are interpretation only (observed test default rates: Low 12.6%, Medium 40.3%, High 73.6%)

leakage_audit: features available at scoring time only (spending: Phase-3 available-at-t whitelist, chronological split by target file; risk: months -6..-1 + static); preprocessing train-only; no target-derived features (Phase-3/Phase-4 audits)
target_description: OBSERVED binary outcome 'default payment next month' (0/1), never rescaled; models are regressors whose continuous output is the predicted default probability (user-approved probability-anchored design, 2026-10-08). RiskScore_0_100 = 100 x predicted probability is an interpretation, NOT a separately trained target.
output_semantics: predicted probability of default next month in [0, 1]; multiply by 100 for the 0-100 risk score; bands are interpretation only (observed test default rates: Low 12.6%, Medium 40.3%, High 73.6%)

split.mechanism: stratified 60/20/20, seed 42 (cross-sectional snapshot: one row per customer, single common prediction date - no temporal ordering to break; 30,000 unique IDs make entity leakage impossible)

last_state_rule_PAY_0.note: persistence-analog; true time-series persistence NOT_APPLICABLE (one row per customer)

selection: best supervised model by validation Brier (0.13726); beats prevalence and last-state baselines (Phase-4 report section 12)
caveats: UCI data = Taiwan credit-card clients, 2005; generalization to other populations/products is uncertain - decision-support, not an automatic score
R2 on a bounded binary outcome is inherently small; Brier/AUC vs the prevalence baseline are the meaningful yardsticks
the 61-100 High band is legitimately sparse at 22.12% prevalence
repay_ratio_mean6 NaN is structural (zero billed total); handled inside the pipeline by median imputation + missing indicator, never zero-filled
